title: Joining Nat Cole in June 1953
summary: Lee accepted Nat's offer after several calls, opening at the Blue Note in Chicago and La Vie en Rose, then recording Twisted Stockings and Mona Lisa.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: I joined him in June of '53. He had called several times, and I really didn't want to travel. I didn't want to travel. So he finally made me an offer I couldn't refuse, okay? And the first date I had with him was at the Blue Note in Chicago; this was when he had not quite arrived yet, you know, and we played the Blue Note in Chicago, and that was a well known jazz place. And I think we played there, like 3 weeks, and we went from there to La Vie en Rose in New
York, you know, the La Vie en Rose was a small club, also.

And then we came back home -- they sent for us to come in; they had a hit record for us. They had a hit song for us. You know -- come off the road, you got to record this. So they bring us here, go to Capitol Records to record a thing called "Twisted Stockings" -- "Twisted Stockings" was what we came to record, and on the same day, we did "Mona Lisa", so nobody ever remembers 'Twisted Stockings', you know whatever happened to "Twisted Stockings" -- no one had ever heard of the song, but that was what we came in to do.
I think that when we started recording with the strings, like "Too Young" and "Unforgettable" -- those things, when we came back, we played Cyros when Cyros was going.
